name: Elaine Alcázar
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember watching my daughter search a crowd for both familiar faces.” On Tuesday, near Juniper Street, Elaine knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I want my little girl to see grown men making room without one of them having to disappear.
appearance: Elaine is easy to recognize by a center part and straight chestnut hair and heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw. Usually dressed in a cream pullover with a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining, Elaine steadies a cup with both hands while listening when listening.
personality: Elaine treats a small promise with the gravity others reserve for a contract. This makes Elaine lovely to rely on and surprisingly difficult to invite on a whim.
agenda: To show the younger child two adults making room.
family: Taylor Beck is Elaine’s older relative by marriage. Elaine is free to hang up first. Taylor makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The widow's dividend*, Taylor says, “I want the first dividend in cash to tip the woman who cleaned our first office.”
connections: Frankie Armas. The younger child gets to watch a turn another student wants to learn.
